Change Portugal from Galleon to Grenadier (Cacador), Maya from Spearman to Worker (Quick Worker), make iWorkRate visible in Sevopedia Unit and Unit button hover

- UNIT_PORTUGAL_CARRACK: replace Portugal's map-dependent Carrack/Galleon naval UU with UNIT_PORTUGAL_CACADOR, a Grenadier land UU. Keep the generic Grenadier's 12 strength, 120-hammer cost, +25% vs Gun, +10% city attack and light collateral package; add free Combat III, +1 chance first strike, 25% withdrawal instead of 20%, Grass +10% attack/defense and Forest +10% attack/defense. Combat III is the main enduring perk so veteran Portuguese units are less likely to waste the UU bonus on an already-owned low Combat rank and can carry it into later upgrades; the smaller intrinsic effects give the Caçador a light-infantry/skirmisher identity without overloading raw strength. Coincidentally, both start with "ca" which is funny (and both units started with a "G" (Galleon in AdvCiv-SAS before removal) but anyway).
- As a result of the Netherlands East Indiaman and Portugal Carrack replacements, playable civilizations currently have no naval civ-specific units: naval UUs can be effectively absent on land-heavy maps or disproportionately important on naval-heavy maps unless enough comparable naval counterparts exist.
- UNIT_MAYA_HOLKAN: replace Maya's Holkan Spearman UU with UNIT_MAYA_QUICK_WORKER, a Worker UU. Pacal/Maya have often underperformed or lost early in autoplay, while both the very weak base Civ4/AdvCiv Holkan and the later SAS Spearman/skirmisher attempt remain a narrow early military identity with a short usefulness window; the culture-oriented Ball Court is also relatively specialized rather than a broad compensating power spike. The Quick Worker instead strengthens Maya more generally and keeps Pacal strategically versatile: keep the generic Worker's 50-hammer cost, 2 movement and normal movement rules, but raise work rate from 100 to 125 (+25%), helping resource connection, roads, tile development, chopping, expansion, economy, wonder building or military logistics. This fits Maya intensive agriculture/infrastructure and organized labor, stays distinct from India's terrain-cost immunity and the Dutch Swift Worker's extra movement, and loosely echoes Civ3's worker-oriented Agricultural/Industrious Maya and Javelin Thrower Enslave mechanic.

- Worker unit-info visibility: show each builder unit's base `iWorkRate` from `CIV4UnitInfos.xml` directly as `Work Rate: X%` through shared unit help in both Sevopedia Unit special abilities and normal unit hover help, replacing the relative-vs-default comparison so the Quick Worker, Barbarian Worker and other Worker variants are immediately distinguishable; keep technology/civic/building build-speed modifiers as a separate Sevopedia line.

Simplify (mostly nerf as was too swingy and sometimes OP) and rebalance terrain/feature/geography effects and otherwise units more generally, add a corresponding doc section in README_Assets_Rebalancing.md, Improve light source ZIP snapshot context and Git metadata, buff UNIT_OTTOMAN_JANISSARY and other changes

- Rebalanced unit terrain/feature modifiers toward gameplay rather than full historical simulation: Terrain and Hills now use 10/20% tiers with an absolute 20% cap because they can affect city combat; Features use 10/20/40% tiers because cities remove features; City modifiers remain separately balanced. Generic units normally use lighter values, while civ-specific units can use the stronger tier when the specialization is part of their identity.
- Corrected terrain/feature defense on units with `bNoDefensiveBonus`: unintended positive explicit terrain/feature defense no longer broadly bypasses the intended defensive limitation. The generic Camel Archer deliberately retains only +10% Desert defense as a small specific identity exception; mounted/camel/elephant and relevant civ-specific units otherwise lose positive terrain/feature defense where it conflicted with their role.
- Moved the cross-cutting terrain/feature combat rationale out of the civ-specific-unit roster into a dedicated documentation section, and expanded that section into concise generic-unit and civ-specific-unit terrain/feature rosters so the current values and their balance intent can be reviewed in one place without overwriting each UU's main gameplay rationale.
- Tightened the terrain review with a focused-specialization guideline: every combat-capable civ-specific unit keeps at least one deliberate terrain or feature identity; Hills/Peaks are plot types and can complement that identity separately, while its added positive terrain package normally uses one strong 20% terrain or at most two weak 10% terrains; relevant generic-unit affinities/weaknesses can carry through or be strengthened, while feature bonuses remain a separate, narrower budget.
- For the shared balance rules, historical/thematic reasoning and exact current terrain/feature packages, see README_Assets_Rebalancing.md (Unit terrain and feature combat modifiers). The entries below record what changed in this pass rather than repeating the full rationale.

Note: the current balance is a tamer but more balanced and sometimes more varied (e.g., new Sumerian Vulture Flood Plains effect) version of the old AdvCiv-SAS terrain/feature and such effects, done with the help of ChatGPT-5.6-Sol (i mostly only reviewed or gave a few ideas a bit or such) thanks.

commit 39eab367845417860483f5c34d2b81d9fcd227aa
Author: f1rpo <hidden>
Date:   2026-08-09 10:02:44 +0200

Tweak AI target for floating defenders when unit spending high

Based on this SAS commit:
https://github.com/wonderingabout/AdvCiv-SAS/commit/2be4fd2642f193dd11df172eb97ac08b919cbb09

That commit halves the target for floating defenders or even divides it by three when unit spending is clearly above the desired (aspirational) cap. I've gone with a reduction to 72% floating defenders. This does not result in unit deletions, to be clear; the AI just won't train more floating defenders when unit spending is too high (unless in a land war). When I monitored the effect for 250 turns on AI Auto Play, it looked beneficial; saved the AI from producing a few units that it had no need for anyway. As before, production of floating defenders is fully suspended when in financial trouble. [advc.107]

commit aa81ff32c2d9c22e2c0cc9ff8a214f81398eaad3
Author: f1rpo <hidden>
Date:   2026-07-19 20:33:37 +0200

Fix degraded performance of PerfectMongoose

Fixes commit a61a76dc. One wonders if the peculiar use of a circle instead of a disk had been intentional after all. A disk of this size (20 squares radius) really isn't easily possible without a very noticeable performance penalty. So I've shrunk the disk and tweaked the code. Still probably takes a couple of seconds, i.e. the Smooth call, and the Deviate call (7-square radius) also isn't harmless.

The smoothing is used for the temperature maps (one for summer, one for winter; later, monsoon effects are derived from this two-season model). Temperatures are derived from latitude and land/ sea status. I suppose that latter criterion being binary creates a need for some wide-area smoothing. [advc.021b]

I've thrown in some test code too. If need be, the smoothing could be done more efficiently by reusing results of adjacent plots -- they're derived mostly from the same disk, just shifted by one row or column. The tests can then come in handy for validation.

Fix AI workers executing queued mission in wrong plot

201150ab61534364caaca3bc2c25ea49def1177d
... added the activateHeadMission call that occurs after a move-to or route-to mission has failed. However, it seems that the base game made the same call via deleteMissionQueueNode, so I would guess that this problem has been in the game all along.

commit 1a3aea9ad01407dd290aa470b46202fe83e1bb3d
Author: f1rpo <hidden>

Fix another bug in use of asset values for AI city evac decision

The earlier, recent bugfix was in the percentile rank calculation:
commit 4392e521. Turns out that the ranks had also been used incorrectly. The percentile rank of a score, to quote Wikipedia, is "the percentage of scores [...] that are less than that score." So, while one might think that a high (i.e. good) score implies a low (i.e. good) rank, the highest score actually corresponds to 100% or something close to that. Adopted from the SAS mod: commit
https://github.com/wonderingabout/AdvCiv-SAS/commit/e466b86faa145a17749e77ef1021d0da6afbfb6c

* Add initial AIP predump checker and workflow step

Add an initial workflow build check for Sevopedia Leader AI Personality predump values. The new checker reconstructs a partial set of effective values from CIV4LeaderHeadInfos.xml by applying LEADER_DEFAULTS inheritance, CvLeaderHeadInfo missing-tag defaults, and UWAI personality scaling, then compares them against the committed predumped cache.

This first implementation validates direct scalar getters, scalar attitude-threshold getters, Flavors, and NoWarAttitudeProbs. Contact and memory aggregate values are intentionally left for a later shared-helper refactor because those predump entries are AIP-derived aggregate fields rather than direct XML/DLL array values.

- This keeps the existing iAggregatedRaw* and iAggregated* cache key names, but clarifies the layer boundary: synthetic raw contact/memory fields are created before normalization, then reused by the normal AIP ranking/cache pipeline and by the XML/UWAI predump checker.

Collapse C++ signatures returns statements (#27)

* Collapse safe C++ function signatures to one line (add `collapse_cpp_signatures.py`)
- **C++ signature cleanup:** collapsed **safe multiline C++ function declarations/definitions** to one physical line across the DLL source, making **signatures easier to grep, compare, and review** in diffs/LLM-assisted passes. Done with the help of the new [`collapse_cpp_signatures.py`](/LLM_Helpers/README.md#collapse_cpp_signaturespy), a **conservative** signature-only helper, which intentionally skips ordinary multiline calls and unsafe comments, while also supporting traceable hoisting for reviewed whole-line comments inside signatures; review its output as a mechanical source-cleanup tool rather than a general C++ formatter. It was empirically idempotent after the first full DLL pass (rerunning reported no safe C++ signature collapses found). This is especially useful for **overloaded functions** like `void addMessage`, or e.g., `void CvDeal::endTrade(TradeData trade, PlayerTypes eFromPlayer, PlayerTypes eToPlayer, bool bTeam, /* advc.036: */ bool bUpdateAttitude, PlayerTypes eCancelPlayer) // advc.130p`, instead of its old three-line equivalent.

commit b9ccb1be872e47d8b9c1f655f5b7c8f82dadc457
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-06-18 11:49:40 +0200

(Fixed) Likely inherited AI upgrade-budget issue: normal upgrades could overshoot the remaining budget and leave the AI almost broke (See KI#160)
- **AI unit upgrades - stop routine upgrades from draining the treasury:** Fixes an AI spending problem where normal unit **upgrades could overshoot the intended upgrade budget**. Previously, the AI only checked whether it was still below budget before starting the next upgrade, but did not check whether that next upgrade itself fit the remaining budget. For example, in BBAI diagnostics, an AI with 280 gold reserved for upgrades could spend 237 gold, still count as under budget, then start another 237 gold upgrade and end up spending 474 gold total, sometimes leaving only a few gold in the treasury. Routine **upgrades now check the actual remaining upgrade budget before upgrading**. **Emergency**-style upgrades, such as important city defenders or special impassable-unit upgrades, **remain more flexible**, but normal upgrades are much less likely to waste all available gold. AIs in **financial trouble also avoid** routine upgrades **unless they are focused on war**. See KI#160.

commit bd9c02aac4d56d35291c39f2a794eccd47141e5c
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-06-17 16:23:25 +0200

Fixed Base AdvCiv issue: ready AI attack-capable stacks ignored nearby barbarian cities without normal war targets (See KI#158)
- **AI attack stacks now opportunistically capture nearby barbarian cities:** before this fix, ready city-attack-capable (i.e. not just `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY`) stacks could sit idle because the AI had **no normal war target yet**, even with a **nearby pathable barbarian city**. Now, if the AI has **no normal target** and is **not already busy with an active war**, the stack can **attack that barbarian city instead**. This does not override normal wars or normal war targets; it fills the no-target idle gap. This change is usually a **strong** move: barbarian cities are often weak, cost little diplomatically, and capturing them can give land, population, resources, unit support, and future growth without spending a settler or interrupting city production nor growth. In the tested save before the fix, nearby barbarian cities survived at game end at ~T400 despite reachable AI armies to Napoleon and Shaka, and barbarian being very weak in comparison, yet bonuses-rich, and Shaka was among weakest players; after the fix, Zulu captured Hurrian at T127, Alemanni at T132, Visigoth at T148, and Gaul at T153, turning those nearby barb cities into an early expansion boost and making Shaka the strongest player for almost all middle game and end game, almost allowing him to win. This change should make AI significantly stronger. See KI#158

commit 42cbc76648165ee979dae223a4374b3884e404a9
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-06-16 10:42:44 +0200

Reduce AI worker lower-food improvement oscillation and multi-oscillation
- **Worker lower-food replacement guard:** from a **tunable era onward** (default as of now: Medieval), AI workers no longer replace existing **no-bonus** improvements with lower-food alternatives. This targets **repeated food-threshold oscillation** such as **Farm → Cottage → Farm → Cottage** or **Mine → Windmill → Mine** after the city briefly looks food-safe. It still allows equal-food retools, food-restoration changes such as Cottage → Farm, and cleanup of City Ruins or obsolete/non-active improvements. In the tested BBAI log, the worst Mali farm/cottage loops reached Farm again and then skipped later Farm → Cottage attempts from about T128/T130 onward. This change is because before this era, cities are often small or health/happiness-capped (extra/excess food may not necessarily help or could be inefficient early) and early cottages still have time to mature, but later, cities are usually larger, health sources are generally multiple, and specialist yields are stronger than plot yields (so any food can be used and is generally strong/stronger), and cottages/growth improvements have less time to grow and pay back, so preserving food support is usually stronger.

commit a9515bf013262e4958c7a8d01e0635a36786fdd8
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-06-15 21:15:20 +0200

Fixed Base AdvCiv issue: ready city-attack AI stacks could park for future upgrades (sometimes for a very long time) in non-faraway cities too, even when no unit could upgrade now (See KI#156)
This expands on previous KI#155 fix, but we now observed the same pattern happens in our core cities too, not just faraway ones.

**Ready attack stacks stop parking for unavailable upgrades:** if a city-attack stack is ready, the target is not too strong, and **0 units can upgrade now**, the AI now keeps moving toward the target instead of waiting for possible future upgrades. This fixes real offensive freezes: in one BBAI-log sample, USA Washington waited from **T147-T181** with up to **59 units / 69% of total military** while targets were only **3-5 turns** away; Mali Gao waited from **T233-T255** with up to **42 units / 41% of total military**. The AI still waits for real immediate upgrades: a USA Seattle stack waited while **6 units could upgrade now**, then attacked/moved once that number became **0**. This is thought to be much stronger, because it uses the current military advantage before enemies catch up; old units can be spent in war instead of sitting around draining upkeep, needing future upgrade gold (solved if they die as well), and risking obsolescence; successful captures can then increase economy, unit support, and long-term growth; and the needless wait was very problematic and inefficient too.

commit e64fa7ceffb0a129d9049a329c1cc68a169b0efc

Further restrict AI scrapping rules, now and as of now only to sufficiently obsolete units; Add Assets DLL GitHub workflow check

- Add XML SAS define for fully disabling AI scrapping (currently disabled)
- Add one for limiting it to obsolete units after an ObsoleteTech-era delay. Keep cargo-capable units protected and improve scrap diagnostics with separate SCRAP_DECISION and SCRAP_EVENT log lines. The rationale is that only very outdated units are no longer useful enough to justify their clutter or upkeep; until then, keeping units is usually better than short-term financial relief from scrapping, because they can defend cities, deter attacks, pressure rivals, or be spent in war. War can also reduce excess units naturally, and successful captures can increase unit support, economy, and long-term growth more than deleting troops would. So this strict-but-not-absolute new scrapping gate is believed to be stronger for AI.

commit b45eb19a0a45fee7e75c7a1ecb0856a4d98c3dac
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-06-14 09:18:25 +0200

Fix/reduce and enhance AI workers abandoning current best local plot to move away to next city to improve: improve first if you can
When small cities were considered improved enough, workers could rotate away even while standing on a useful owned/workable BFC plot, such as a forest that should be chopped or improved. These would then be roaded only or not improved at all despite standing on them, and they would be left unimproved even much later in the game.

Keep the worker local only when AI_bestCityBuild itself selects the current plot as the best local build, preserving city-to-city worker rotation without duplicating worker build logic. This greatly reduces these unimproved or roaded-only forest plot instances.

- UNIT_SCANDINAVIA_VIKING: TerrainAtk SNOW 50->35; TerrainDef TUNDRA 25->10; TerrainDef SNOW 50->10. Keeps the Viking more offense/raider-focused while reducing overly strong cold-terrain defensive camping (Similar reasoning as as of now for the Hajjan).
- UNIT_RUSSIA_COSSACK: TerrainAtk SNOW 50->35; TerrainDef TUNDRA 35->10; TerrainDef SNOW 50->25. Keeps cold-weather resistance/flavor, but reduces overly broad defensive strength on a mostly mobile/offensive unit (Similar reasoning as as of now for the Hajjan).
- UNIT_BYZANTINE_CATAPHRACT: TerrainDef GRASS 25->10. Keeps grassland attack flavor, but reduces defensive spike on an already high-strength mounted unit.
- UNIT_EGYPTIAN_WAR_CHARIOT: TerrainAtk DESERT 35->25; TerrainDef DESERT 35->10. Base strength is already high enough for such an early unit, so desert bonuses stay moderate.
- UNIT_SPANISH_CONQUISTADOR: TerrainDef PLAINS 25->10. Keeps plains attack/offensive identity while reducing broad defensive value.
- UNIT_SUMERIAN_VULTURE: TerrainDef DESERT 25->10; TerrainDef GRASS 25->10. Keeps terrain flavor while reducing defensive camping value.
- UNIT_NATIVE_AMERICA_DOG_SOLDIER: TerrainDef DESERT 25->10. Keeps desert/terrain flavor while reducing defensive camping value.
- UNIT_ROMAN_LEGIONARY: also TerrainDef PLAINS 25->10, in addition to free PROMOTION_COMBAT1->PROMOTION_COMBAT2.
- Update docs.

This fits England's more defensive/economic early profile while still allowing aggressive use for thematic and strategic variety.". - We deliberately do not preserve the whole Military Advisor across full close/reopen: testing `screen.setPersistent(True)` there made very large late-game Battles histories faster to reopen, but broke Civ4's native minimap lifecycle, causing the Map tab to reopen as an empty blue panel and also break after debug-mode transitions until save reload. So the Battles cache is kept for tab switching only, while full Military Advisor close/reopen rebuilds the screen/minimap for reliability. See also KI#129 (Update).

commit 05174d6206304e62983b85614ab44bbc73e21420
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-05-22 12:39:39 +0200

mostly generalize direct map grid-size tables after ARENA shift
as per GPT-5.5's review:

Already handled in this diff
Direct getGridSize dictionaries in BTG_Grid, BTG_Lagoon, Earth2, SAS_Longworld, plus the generic template in CvMapGeneratorUtil. Those were the risky ones because they index runtime eWorldSize directly.

Likely OK / not urgent
Percent-scaling maps like Pangaea, Terra, Hemispheres, Tectonics, Mixed_Continents, not_too_Big_or_Small. These usually use getNumPlotsPercent, so XML provides the base size and the dict is only a modifier. They may be semantically shifted, but the result remains plausible and changing them should be tested map-by-map, not swept in blindly.

Needs separate review if we want to be exhaustive
Rainforest, Global_Highlands grain tables, Earth2 grain table, RandomScriptMap. These are not direct dimensions, but they still use runtime getWorldSize() or similar keys for terrain/grain behavior. A shift there can affect climate/shape rather than map size. Worth a separate commit if we care.

also in this commit:

-  Fix SAS_Longworld.py key error when world size is Huge (was too small and incorrect at this world size too). Minor grid size adjustments (SAS48 is preserved as compared to before, standard world size also seems empirically fairly well spaced. World sizes have been adjusted with the help of GPT-5.5 so they have about the same per default ratio, so i'm thinking other worldsizes likely didn't shift too much as compared to before).

commit 4a2c6394d1d4add7ac1c0e2f094413e299912295
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-05-21 11:46:36 +0200

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/1.12' into updated-tech-rework
- updated default 48 civs DLL, and 18 civs DLL
- autoplay tested to seemingly run fine end to end on a sas24 pangea map in one go (win at t392, no crash), and other 0 to 100 and 0 to 200 autoplay runs on perfect mongoose
- note: perfect mongoose takes significantly longer to load, didn't measure but maybe 2x or more like 3x-4x or such longer

notes (claude code opus 4.7's review):
3. ~2x slower load — expected, it's inherent to this fix (not your error)
The old getCirclePoints returned only the circle outline (~8·r points). The fix switches the averaging functions to getFilledCirclePoints, which returns the filled disc (~π·r² points). Those run per-tile in Smooth/Deviate (width×height calls), so per-tile work went from O(r) to O(r²) → big map-gen slowdown. That's the cost of sampling the full neighborhood for a correct average instead of just the ring. Your port is right; the slowdown is upstream's trade-off. Worth noting in your changelog so it's not mistaken for a regression later.

enhance battles tab
as per GPT-5.5's answer thx:

Changes:

- Effective max strength no longer gets invented from XML when combat-log strength is unknown. Unknown current and unknown max now both stay blank.
- Added separate base/XML strength columns for attacker and defender: STRb, STRc, STRm.
- Current strength coloring now uses:
- white only at full effective strength
	green above 66%
	yellow above 33%
	red at 33% or below
- Updated the LOG output to include base strength too.
- You probably do not need to regenerate saves for this UI change:
	Base strength is computed live from XML.
	The old invented max value was UI fallback only, so existing rows should display more honestly now.
	Only genuinely missing combat-log data will remain blank, as intended.
- I also trimmed table widths. The saved width goes back into attacker/defender unit-name columns.

commit db46a59ae5873aa2f7a21b387e1fe2697b010b45
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-04-24 00:44:52 +0200

adjust sevopedia groupings logic for eventtrigger so era are better taken into account
as per claude code opus 4.7 thanks a lot:

Those diagnostics are hints about pre-existing unused parameters (bSortLists across many grouping functions, unpackMusicKey) that were there before my changes touched this file — they're part of API contracts callers depend on, not something I introduced. Leaving them alone.

Summary of what I did this round:

Rewrote _SAS_getEventTriggerEarliestEra to factor in all era-gating fields instead of just <OrPreReqs>/<AndPreReqs>:
OR-tech list → min era (any single tech satisfies) — unchanged
AND-tech list → max era (all must be known)
<OtherPlayerHasTech> — was missing, this is what Airliner Crash uses
<CivicPrereq> → civic's getTechPrereq() era
<BuildingsRequired> → each BuildingClass's default building's getPrereqAndTech() era
<UnitsRequired> → UnitClass default unit's getPrereqAndTech() era
<ReligionsRequired> → religion's getTechPrereq() era
<CorporationsRequired> → corporation's getTechPrereq() era
Routes skipped (use TechMovementChanges list, no clean single-era answer; rare anyway)
Two small extracted helpers _SAS_getBuildingClassEra / _SAS_getUnitClassEra so chain-lookup is readable
Algorithm combines them correctly: trigger can't fire before max(min(OR), max(all AND-ish constraints))
Returns -1 only when truly nothing era-gates the trigger
Airliner Crash should now land in Modern (via OtherPlayerHasTech=TECH_FLIGHT). Expect the "Any era" bucket to shrink noticeably and late-era buckets (Industrial/Modern/Atomic) to grow once you relaunch.

commit 923840f152dc0045b696f0993f8dbf0bc3301308
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-02-23 15:35:45 +0100

(Tremendously Improved) Do not buy dominated or equivalent strategic bonuses (era and bonus-aware)
- **Do not buy dominated or equivalent strategic bonuses (era and bonus-aware):** strategic resource buying now uses explicit exclusion rules, so AI skips dominated/equivalent offers instead of considering them as valid buys. Examples: in Classical, Copper is not needed if we have Iron; in Classical metals and mounted lines can substitute each other so redundant buys are skipped; Horse and Camel are treated as equivalent in Classical/Medieval/Renaissance; in Industrial (before Modern), Horse has the edge (no Camel Dragoon), so Camel is skipped if Horse is already available, etc. Change in `CvPlayerAI::AI_bonusTrade`. See KI#109.

balance changes and code enhancements
- UNIT_MODERN_INFANTRY: PROMOTION_FIRST_STRIKE1 (previous base advciv was was PROMOTION_AMPHIBIOUS, but not needed at all since unit is strong enough already or doesn't fit thematically in advciv-sas)
- fix leaders **inconsistently not having 150** as the **total of their BBAI victory weights**: (iCultureVictoryWeight, iSpaceVictoryWeight, iConquestVictoryWeight, iDominationVictoryWeight, iDiplomacyVictoryWeight, 150): (`LEADER_BISMARCK`, 20, 25, 25, 30, 40, 140) -> 20, 25, 25, 35, 45, 150; (`LEADER_BRENNUS`, 0, 30, 30, 50, 30, 140) -> 0, 30, 35, 55, 30, 140; (`LEADER_LINCOLN`, 10, 35, 35, 15, 45, 140) -> 10, 40, 35, 15, 50, 150; (`LEADER_RAMESSES`, 25, 25, 35, 35, 20, 140) -> 35, 25, 35, 35, 20, 150.
- starting techs changes (for starting tech counts and combos counts see sevopedia tech or assets rebalancing doc):
	- - Arabia: Mysticism + Pottery → Hunting + Mysticism; Desert pastoral/tribal-warrior flavor + smooth path toward Animal Husbandry/camels; Mysticism preserves religion/culture identity (and your UB is university-based so no Pottery dependency).
	- - Greece: Fishing + Mysticism → Mining + Mysticism; Keeps the “culture/religion” signal (temples/oracles/cults) while also pushing the Hoplite → Bronze/Iron line sooner via Mining; better matches “bronze + sacred polis” as a starter identity.
	- - Holy Roman: Hunting + Mysticism → Mysticism + Pottery; Reads more like “Church + towns/guild/urban administration” than generic hunting, and unlocks their civ-specific building (Courthouse-based) sooner via the Pottery line.
	- - Kingdom of Benin: Fishing + Mysticism → Mysticism + Pottery; Pottery anchors the “fortified/urban builder court-state” + supports your Impluvium/aqueduct line; Mysticism keeps the ritual/court legitimacy flavor (and avoids pushing them toward early bronze play).
	- - Korea: Mining + Mysticism → Fishing + Mining; Keeps Mining (the more distinctive “Korea-coded” pillar: metals/engineering), and adds Fishing to reflect a peninsula/coastal civilization with strong maritime/trade exposure—without implying an early religion-race start.
- add index / leader name pairs in SevoPediaLeaderCachePredumped.py, remove excess blank lines, and line separate leaders and fields

commit d9e8051723393d41e88479d9624dd13d524383e7
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>

(Tremendously Improved) Fix or heavily reduce weird back and forth of declaring war then quickly withdrawing without city attack
- **Minimum Stack size before war**: Added a minimum stack unit count requirement to prevent the stack from being marked as "ready" until it has enough units: no `MOVE_DECLARE_WAR` flag, no premature advance toward the city, and AI keeps building units until the stack is big enough. Helps fix the issue of "back and forth" war declarations with immediate retreat without city attack: low-numbered unit stacks were especially sensible to power swings (city defenses, one more enemy units skews win chance, etc.). Change in `CvUnitAI::AI_attackCityMove`. See KI#104

commit 4f7a13df9cae48b82ed30261719552f37fcc5c35
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-02-02 12:27:51 +0100

update docs about pre-AdvCiv-SAS scenarios not being supported in AdvCiv-SAS
- Scenarios: "Play a Scenario" and "Custom Scenario" in the main menu shows some scenario files that are pre-AdvCiv-SAS; since we made structural changes like renaming `_CORN` to `_MAIZE`, adding `CAMEL_BONUS`and many other changes, pre-AdvCiv-SAS scenarios are not supported in AdvCiv-SAS. Also, we cannot just grey in the main menu (via `NoCustomScenario = 1` in [AdvCiv-SAS.ini](/AdvCiv-SAS.ini)) these play modes in case player add AdvCiv-SAS compatible scenarios that they would be unable to then play; plus this does not fix "Play a Scenario", only "Custom Scenarios", so preferred to just document it as an all around much better and simpler solution.

addresses player feedback at https://forums.civfanatics.com/threads/advciv-sas-simple-advanced-strategy.699716/post-16916237

Revamp Main interface; fix Base AdvCiv bug of obsolete GP rate not displayed but counted on hover in GP bar
A bit more changes than what we did here, but easier to take from the main changes guide directly:

- **Main Interface (Common)**: Moved **minimap to the right-edge** for quicker read. Add **details** to most **progress bars**; e.g. in the Tech bar `Fusion: 2245 / 5774 (35)`. Show **chars in the GP bar even if 100%** (e.g. `Great Scientist: Lyons (3) - [RESEARCH_CHAR] 100%`) Change in [GPUtil.py](/Assets/Python/BUG/GPUtil.py) and [CvMainInterface.py](/Assets/Python/Screens/CvMainInterface.py). See [Main interface rework](/README.md#main-interface-rework).
- **Main Interface (City Screen)**: Enhanced with a new **Great Person +n ICON** information in relevant Buildings' rows; added a new **Specialists Breakdown** and **Culture Breakdown**; added **optional extra rows** in the **Production Chooser Bar** and **optionally hide the unit bar** (`"PlotListPanel"`) (note: does not affect the production chooser outside of the city screen); added **Buttons** (i.e. icons) in the **Production Queue**; fixed some hard anchored items that now **dynamically** adjust to sides' width. **Beautified** it as well: removed the 3 gray bars ("Trade Routes", "Buildings", "Specialists"), increased sides' width, made bonuses columns even in width, and other changes. These changes allow to now display more information and reduce the need for scrolling or hovering. Also **enlarged** the **Bottom-Left** and **Bottom-Right** panels so they align dynamically with the enlarged **Side Panels**. Enhanced the **city bar** and **other bars**, e.g., `Lakamha: 16 - 12372 (4500BC)` or `Growing - 30/43 (4 Turns)`. Split the **Draft group** into hurry controls on the right (and a **new draft button**) and config options on the right. Add building list filtering buttons ("Show All Buildings", "Show Regular Buildings Only", "Show National Wonders Only", "Show World Wonders Only"). And other changes. Change in [CvMainInterface.py](/Assets/Python/Screens/CvMainInterface.py). See also KI#101.
- **Main Interface (Map View)**: **Reordered buttons** (end turn, city change arrows) and wrapped them in a **pretty panel**. Added buttons to unit stack, selected unit.

Add new ObsoleteTech optional XML field for units
- New **optional XML field**: `ObsoleteTech` **for units**: if set, this unit **can no longer be produced once we have discovered this tech** (e.g. Ancient Maceman (`UNIT_WARRIOR`) obsolete at `TECH_BRONZE_WORKING`). This XML field is **optional**: if **not set** (`<ObsoleteTech>NONE</ObsoleteTech>`, e.g. for the `UNIT_SETTLER`) or missing entirely (better **inter-mod portability**), a **fallback default of `NONE`** is provided anyway, so the unit is never obsolete, meaning no tech discovery will stop allowing to produce it (base AdvCiv/Civ4 behaviour). This new XML field allows to **avoid unit clutter in later eras** (no more **abherrent obsolete units in later eras** (e.g. Ancient Maceman produced in Medieval Era; Pikemen in Industrial Era)) being **produced** or shown in the **Production Chooser Bar**. **AI** becomes **naturally stronger** as a result of these changes. Additionally, this also helps set **clean scrapping rules** to computationally cheaply detect and remove old units for the AI's military compostion, or **further enhancements**. **Sevopedia** Blurbs with links fully implemented in [CvGameTextMgr.cpp](/CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp). See [README: New optional XML fields](/README.md#new-optional-xml-fields-eg-obsoletetech-for-units). See also KI#93.

commit e8659a5e4c4afae41306dfc04e8ec62eeb77eb99
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-01-09 21:00:57 +0100

Change from short to int the Found Value pipeline
- **Found-value** evaluation now uses **`int`** end-to-end (CitySiteEvaluator, AIFoundValue, CvPlot cache, SPI, Python callback), **not `short`**. Why: **avoid overflow/underflow** and short wraparounds in site scoring; keep the logic the same while **improving reliability**. Expectation: more robust site values, fewer edge-case penalties/boosts from short overflow; no known negative gameplay change. Performance: `int` is typically at least as fast as short on modern CPUs; no slowdown expected. Tested: autoplay ran fine. See [Change from short to int the Found value pipeline](/README.md#change-from-short-to-int-the-found-value-pipeline).
Co-authored-by: <GPT-Codex-5.2 codex@openai.com>

commit ba5517013b1d3c22afc3585901ed8d09862b0d87
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2026-01-08 00:36:14 +0100

refactor sevopedia charts; possibly fix handicap and world size charts based on the working game speed chart
- Gamespeed's calendar maintains the same in-theme reordering (e.g. 01 is always the first and 02 always the second), but handicap and game speed have their in theme order vary. Inter-theme war is sitll before the other themes.

Not sure and i didn't check if it was the case before this commit, but while refactoring the issue emerged; fixed with the very nice help of chatgpt 5.2 thanks a lot.

Also refactored them in this commit.

Yep — this is the classic “unstable sort when lots of ties" problem in Civ4 tables.

What’s happening (why it shuffles)
When you sort by the icon column, every row inside a “theme" (same icon) has the exact same cell text (same icon token). Civ4’s table sort does not keep a stable order for ties, so tied rows can permute differently each time you toggle sorting.
Your Game Speed chart avoids this by adding an invisible tie-breaker to the icon cell text, so even rows with the same icon still sort deterministically.

The fix (replicate GameSpeed behavior)
I updated Handicap and World Size to do the same:
	- Remove the old control-char sort codes (1..31)
	- Add the same zero-width unicode “digits" scheme used in GameSpeed
	- Append an invisible key = (icon group + row index) to the icon cell text
	- That keeps:
		- grouping by icon/theme
		- but makes every row’s icon-cell text unique → no more shuffling

Co-authored-by: ChatGPT (GPT-5.2 Thinking) <chatgpt-gpt-5.2-thinking@advciv-sas.invalid>

- `iBaseGrowthThresholdPercent` (base food required to grow a city): **Fixed at 100 on all handicaps.** Rationale: In base AdvCiv this value varies by difficulty to add a **human growth/expansion penalty** (and it can also shift early expansion pacing via settler cost logic tied to the initial growth threshold). Consequence: Removing this scaling makes **high handicaps** (e.g. Deity) **easier for the human player** (faster early growth/expansion than base AdvCiv), and makes **low handicaps** (e.g. Chieftain) **harder for the human player** (less of an early growth/expansion boost).

You already did the big perf win: _cachedTable means the expensive “pull everything from CvHandicapInfo + build rows" work happens once per instance. The main remaining avoidable costs in your current version are small but real:

- _getFieldIconText() rebuilds a huge icon_map dict every call (it is called once per output row when building data).
- _drawTable() parses the <img=...> tag for every icon cell every time the page is drawn, just to rediscover the button path + sort code.
- _drawTable() also re-wraps everything in <font=...> tags each draw.

Below is a drop-in rewrite that keeps behavior the same, but:

- moves all icon/button/glyph definitions into the one-time table build (nothing icon-related stays on self after caching),
- precomputes the icon-column “(text, buttonPath)" tuple so _drawTable() does no tag parsing,
- caches already font-wrapped cell strings so _drawTable() doesn’t do per-cell string building.

commit e81ea035ab3af8a3fc8e231dc0f86fb50eb59d02
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-12-25 05:54:56 +0100

conservative performance optimizations to the keyboard navigation feature
As chatgpt 5.2 explains below (check if accurate, claude opus 4.5 review the change ok and excellent according to it):

That said: the only meaningful O(n) cost you still have with arrows is in SAS_navigateItemList(), because it re-scans self.list on every Up/Down press to rebuild the selectable indices + find current position. On a 2015 CPU this is already fine (lists are usually a few hundred entries), but if you want a safe + reliable micro-optimization, this one is good:

Safe optimization: cache “selectable rows" during placeItems()
What it changes

	- While placeItems() is already looping to draw the table, also build:
		- self.SAS_selectableListIdx: list indices of displayed real items (skips headers/spacers)
		- self.SAS_itemToSelectablePos: maps iItem → position in SAS_selectableListIdx
	- Then SAS_navigateItemList() becomes O(1) per arrow press (no list scanning), while preserving behavior with filtering/headers because the cache is built after filtering rules are applied.

Is this worth it?

	- Correctness risk: low (it’s just caching what you already displayed).
	- Speed gain: small but real (Up/Down becomes constant-time).
	- Compatibility: Python 2.4-safe (no ternaries/comprehensions; I used has_key in the fallback to match old Py2 style, but you can keep idx not in dict if you prefer).

commit 8a13288983ec3e985d67645a803c0f742aa3992a
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-12-17 13:53:23 +0100

(Tremendously Improved) Build very cheap World Wonders ASAP; (Tremendously Improved) Do not Build Barbarian Blocking Wonders past classical era
- Do not build **Anti-Barbarian Border Blocking** (`bBorderObstacle`) **Wonders** (e.g. Great Wall) past a certain **era** (e.g. Classical era, meaning we will not build Great Wall or equivalent wonders from the Medieval and onwards). Change in `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue`.
- Regardless of the aforementioned pre-filtering rules, **cheap World Wonders ASAP** (hammer `iCost` tunable by era in SAS defines). This is because we have prioritized most early hammer towards early urgent growth (settlers, workers, etc.) or military (urgent rush or defense), and the very cheap cost (e.g. Pyramids not yet built Medieval era) make it attractive and worth having ~1-2 less units or similar. Change in `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue`. Note: about Wonders generally, AdvCiv-SAS uses a quite strict low wonder policy, as early settlers and workers are more valuable generally and a stronger choice; plus later on we have little time to build world wonders as we risk being overrun by our rivals and building world wonders for them as they conquer us, which is a poor choice. A mostly Base AdvCiv-like behaviour of AIs building many wonders can be restored in SAS defines by disabling `SAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_WORLD_WONDERS_OPTIMIZE` (e.g. 0 vs 6 wonders at turn 100 in an autoplay sample with vs without it).

Further addresses: https://forums.civfanatics.com/threads/advciv-sas-simple-advanced-strategy.699716/post-16898915

I believe building settlers or workers is generally stronger especially early, so i kept the "optimize" flag enabled. But you can disable it if you want a more wonder-building like behaviour, or maybe rather one of the sub-knobs as you prefer (but it can quickly become a rabbit hole xd so beware i mean.). See below to specifically tune its suboptions rather. Code added with the help of chatgpt 5.2 thanks -->"

In a bit more detail, we don't want to overdo the wonder cost correction, as wonders are not a shopping list of things that must always be built every game in advciv-sas, only options to choose from or not if deemed relevant (fine to ignore many if not a strong move to build them).

But also, considering it more, even if they are a bit too cheap or may be so, there is still a risk of falling behind militarily and being conquered and so ending up just wasting time and building them for our opponent when they conquer us; with that in mind, it would be fine as such, as unit spam is attractive and reliable, but hopefully wonder building is more so and a more valid strategic option/alternative.

If sas human players disble the xml flag, AIs build wonders seemingly normally and players can adjust it as they prefer).

commit 632163dc4b360293e2cf7eaf389bacc843bc44e1
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-12-08 13:05:00 +0100

(Tremendously Improved) Trade more aggressively and much cheaper any tech once 1+ rivals also discover it
- **Aggressive tech trade discounts for widely known techs:** AIs now sell technologies known by ≥1 of their rivals at **heavy discounts** (e.g. 25% of the original cost/value), recognizing that it is better to secure **some gold** immediately via a cheap sale than to hold out and risk getting **0 gold** if a rival sells it first; implemented in `CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal`. To compensate for this higher trading efficiency, **AI research costs** (`iAIResearchPercent`) have been adjusted (reduced/increased at higher/lower difficulties). See KI#83.

Note: i adjusted `iAIResearchPercent` to match these changes:

iAIResearchPercent,124,116,108,100 (noble),92,84,76,68,60
->
iAIResearchPercent,118,112,106,100 (noble),94,88,82,76,70

Which is effective from AdvCiv-SAS 5161 or higher (i.e. not in the as of now latest stable AdvCiv-SAS 5160).

commit 2a453a1f3f0a8eb4ca9be538ec9553c12d49cc1c
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-12-04 12:01:55 +0100

(Tremendously Improved) Value religions mostly based on popular religion among strong rivals, no longer mostly based on who we already like no matter how weak or strong, and other changes
- Add military power weighting to religion valuing, so that AIs no longer (or much less) choose religions mostly based on who they already like no matter how weak or strong, but now mostly based on which religions are popular among the top military power players. The previous valuation used to lead to much worse diplomacy with them (less trades, more wars, etc.), sometimes even being a blunder from a top dog now being suddenly hated by almost everyone else due to a "random" very suboptimal religion change. Note: This valuation also applies to various areas related to how religion is viewed by the AI, according to chatgpt 5.1, such as the evaluation of state-religion-dependent civics, espionage (change a target's religion), trade / demand value of “adopt religion X". Change in `CvPlayerAI::AI_religionValue`. See KI#82.

as recommended by gemini pro 3 and with my own ideas i mean.

commit 9281726c41a85c5ae08b4cc68c4a9d0497ebf3e3
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-11-28 15:55:47 +0100

rework the list of untradeable techs: 8 less, 5 more; + tech tree rework.

remove untradeable (bTrade 0->1):
- TECH_MONARCHY
- TECH_MATHEMATICS
- TECH_FEUDALISM
- TECH_LATER_ABRAHAMISM
- TECH_BROADER_EDUCATION
- TECH_MILITARY_SCIENCE
- TECH_ASSEMBLY_LINE
- TECH_MASS_MEDIA

add untradeable (bTrade 1->0):
- TECH_THE_WHEEL
- TECH_CODE_OF_LAWS
- TECH_ENGINEERING
- TECH_CHIVALRY
- TECH_FASCISM

Goal is to not make techs untradeable unless they are key gameplay knots, or have a big snowball potential. In particular for many science-leaning ones, if they are not key or decisive or at risk of causing obvious or intense snowballing, allow them rather than not, for versatility and to make gameplay less predictable or tedious/repetitive between games, as well as to have a slightly faster tech pace.

This further nerfs the military path, that by itself should yield enough, while still gating some science techs (else whould be op xd and too one-sided towards nerfing military only and not science)

Also, it does not make much sense thematically that techs like broader education, mathematics, mass media, etc., that are about spreading knowledge are not tradeable (unless op or similar then gate it).

Hopefully all in all better as such.

Other changes in this commit:
- change TECH_CHIVALRY's prereqs from TECH_CIVIL_SERVICE AND TECH_DRAMA to TECH_CIVIL_SERVICE AND (TECH_LATER_ABRAHAMISM OR TECH_FEUDALISM) (so that it is available later and for versatility or such)

commit 2cbb1069bfbf7b4381d25c9cb957c186fc417931
Author: wonderingabout <hidden>
Date:   2025-10-08 22:03:37 +0200

fix dual counting bug (as of now was only affecting siege units)
since i don't understand it, here is chatgpt 5's explanation of it, less tedious as such also:

Here’s the 5-liner:
- The old code looped UnitTypes and added getUnitClassCount(eClass) for each match.
- Many types share the same UnitClass (default + UUs like Catapult + Hwacha), so the same class total was added multiple times → double/triple count.
- This affects any civ whenever a class has >1 type defined in the DB — not just Korea — because you still iterate over all types, even ones your civ can’t build.
- It doesn’t bite only when a class has exactly one type across the whole mod.
- Fix: count per UnitClass once (our new code), or keep the type loop but guard with a seenClass set; either way each class contributes once.

remove trait_expansive, overhaul traits for many leaders for accuracy and gameplay relevance or other or not
- in particular, removed trait_expansive: was overlapping with our more general trait_protective (does not just protect defensively in our mod but also more generally protects health too and also has no anarchy (protects political stability more or less)) and empire-expansion related trait_imperalist (settler discount same, but also trade route based scaling yield modifiers), so trait_expansive was redundant. Also, it was among weakest (flat health not so helpful) and hardest to balance (most often weak or some very rare times op) so removed.
- in addition to the above, overhauled all traits with a focus on historical accuracy most importantly, but also gameplay relevance (+/- civ-specific building and unit timing and effects as well) and overall civ theme to a lesser extent, with the help of chatgpt 5 and multiple rounds of review, +/- other AIs or not so much or yes. For example, julius caesar has been changed from organized + imperialist to aggressive + imperialist (war theme and strength), hammurabi has been changed from organized + aggressive to organized + protective (more of an administrator + defensive civ overall), saladin has been changed from protective + spiritual to spiritual + charismatic (more of warmonger in civ4 + historical warmonger and charisma), or isabella has been changed from spiritual + expansive to spiritual + aggressive (very ruthless campaigns). See for the list of all changes with a before vs after comparison as well as rationales the table at [README_Assets_Rebalancing.md#new-state-after-rework-with-rationale--anyways-etc](/_1_AdvCiv-SAS/Docs/README_Assets_Rebalancing.md#new-state-after-rework-with-rationale--anyways-etc). Note: as of now leaders' flavors unchanged for simplicity vs base advciv
- removed trait_expansive related building modifiers (they were the granary and harbor in advciv-sas before, removed as too generic and op plus no good/relevant candidate to replace them in a balanced way)

- removed `UNITAI_CITY_COUNTER` from non-versatile enough units such as the UNIT_MACEMAN, as they are not versatile enough to be reliable city defenders while still being good offense units (too easy to punish with a stack of knight units that are good against them, even a crossbow stack could defeat defending macemen, so use them for offense rather and disable them from here as well as in similar places). The macemen change is from how it was in base advciv though so i focused on it in this commit, but i also undid various advciv-sas changes to unitai related to UNITAI_CITY_COUNTER in xml, hopefully stronger and more relevant/efficient as such while still being versatile enough, which seems to be the case in autoplay (less excess longbowmen, varied composition otherwise).

Fixed and enhanced the issue of AI overbuilding units with defender UNITAIs when it has few cities for the current stage of the game or too much defender UnitAIs in its military composition: hijack next unitAIs to offense or versatile UnitAIs, yields great results ingame and helps fix 36 longbowmen with defender like UnitAIs and only 3 cities at turn 130 or similar, now (in the early game) with a more dynamic composition and better outcomes it seems on this testing sample!)
- Fixed and enhanced the issue of AI overbuilding units with defender UNITAIs when it has few cities for the current stage of the game (so no need to defend that hard, build attackers to expand rather to save on unit cost and leverage unit count advantage + make up for being boxed in or other causes for having low cities) or simply already a majority of units with a defender UNITAI (for example joao ai had 36 longbowmen at turn 130, almost all with UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE but only 3 cities, very very bad and inefficient, causing his downfall due to not devleopping enough and preparing for war instead by having a more versatile UNITAI composition), results may have been much better if some of these units were attacker UNITAI units or versatile UNITAI units rather. Note: active only in the early game as is when most expansion happens and cities are weakest, then later on we don't use this logic anymore to not alter gameplay too much or cause issues, plus cities are defended and handled well enough hopefully by then to not need our management and early correction. See for details KI#53.2.

(Fixed and greatly enhanced) AI valuing for example pig (+1 health) at the same value than maize (+1 health and +1 health from granary = in total + 2 health, much more so should be valued more in trade), by adding a pre-check in CvPlayerAI::AI_bonusTradeVal, so we value these extra effects as soon as our buyer has the tech for these buildings
- Fixed and greatly enhanced issue of AI overvaluing low effect bonuses such as pig (gives only +1 health) that it would value at same price than some higher effect bonuses such as maize (+2 health effectively (+1, then +1 from granary we almost always have)), by adding a pre-check in `CvPlayerAI::AI_bonusTradeVal` so that as soon as our trading partner has the tech, then we assume said party also has granaries in all cities and thus would gain +2 health from maize, then price accordingly. As a result of these changes, AI should undersatnd much better the value for example of its maize or wheat or grapes (from grocer if i'm not mistaken), and value it more in trade in gold per turn, while pig or cattle or such should be valued less, so it should no longer be possible to cheese it and trade suepr aggressively junk or low-value bonuses for high gpt or other bonuses as easily as was (was quite broken tbh) or such. Hopefully leads to stronger AI trading, and fairer AI vs AI trade as well so they don't throw away their nice bonuses to lower value ones even to other AIs. Some bonuses like iron as a result would also be valued less now as they don't have happiness or health from buildings from example, but hopefully its value should still be high enough, and it's maybe fine as such as there are other paths than having iron maybe at least early (else the human player may trade it too easily or something maybe (i am not sure about this change change but maybe it will work out well in overall diplomacy and allow for more startegy rather than easy trade abuse/exploit)). Note: coastal bonuses have a more moderate version of this as we assume many cities are not coastal so they would not gain the building related bonus's extra effect quite often. We count it as such even in water heavy maps (treated the same to simplify), so fish would be worth more than pig (with as of now harbor) but less than maize or wheat for example. See KI#66 for details.

"
example: barbarian specific granary is free with barbarian palace (barbarians only), so:

if currently selected building is:
* barbarian granary: we show in free with that the barbarian granary is free with the barbarian palace button
* generic granary: we show in free with that the generic granary is free with "None" if a barbarian specific palace exists, else if no barbarian palace exists then we show in free with that the generic granary is free with the barbarian palace
* other civ-specific granary (for example incan terrace): we show in free with that the terrace is free with "None", as the incans cannot have the barbarian palace, so they can never have the free granary, but if the incans could have a palace that has a free granary in it, then display this palace instead, else "None"

🧠 Commit: Improve Aggregate Scoring Accuracy via Percentile Normalization
Summary:
This commit replaces the original min-max normalization used for AI aggregate personality scores with a percentile-based normalization approach. This enhances interpretability and fairness by basing each leader's score on their relative standing among all leaders, rather than on raw value magnitude alone.

🌱 Background — For Beginners and New Modders
In the Sevopedia's AI Personality panel, we show scores like "Aggressive," "Peaceful," or "Sneaky" for each leader. These are aggregate scores based on 2–3 raw AI XML attributes (e.g., how likely the AI is to start wars or build units). We convert those raw numbers into a score between 0 and 100, and then display that score with symbols (like ###) and numbers.

Previously, we used a simple method called min-max normalization to calculate those scores. But this led to scores that were hard to interpret, and sometimes even misleading.

🧪 What Was Wrong Before — The Min-Max Limitation
Previously, the system calculated scores like this:

python
Copy
Edit
score = int((value - min) / (max - min) * 100)
This means that:

The highest value in the entire leader pool always scored 100

The lowest always scored 0

Everyone else was stretched proportionally between those two extremes

🚫 But this approach had issues:

A few extreme outliers could flatten the middle scores

Most leaders would end up clumped around 20–40 even if they were noticeably different in behavior

It made it harder to spot real differences (especially in overlapping traits)

✅ What Changed — Percentile-Based Scoring
Now, we score aggregates by computing each leader’s percentile rank relative to other leaders:

If Boudica has a higher "Aggressive" score than 90% of all leaders, she gets a score of 90

This better reflects how unusual or extreme a leader is compared to their peers.

🔍 Technically:

We gather all leaders’ scores for each aggregate

Sort them from lowest to highest

Assign each leader a score based on how many leaders they outperform (percentile)

Example calculation for Boudica:

python
Copy
Edit
There are 53 leaders.
Boudica ranks 50th in Aggressive out of 53 → (50 / 52) * 100 = ~96 percentile
🔁 Example Before vs After
Gandhi vs Boudica — "Aggressive" Aggregate
Leader	Old Score (Min-Max)	New Score (Percentile)
Gandhi	33	4
Boudica	36	96
🔥 Before, both seemed equally "aggressive" (33 vs 36).
Now, Gandhi is clearly among the least aggressive, and Boudica among the most.

This reflects player expectations better and matches in-game behavior more intuitively.

💡 Why Percentiles Are Better
More Fair: Each score tells you "how many leaders are below this one"

Easier to Understand: 90 means top 10%, 10 means bottom 10%

Less Skewed by Outliers: A few extreme leaders no longer distort the whole scale

🧑‍💻 Technical Summary — For Advanced Users
New method implemented in cache_ai_aggregate_scores()

Each aggregate is precomputed at module load using percentile rank

Sorting of aggregate scores ensures stability and reproducibility

Maintains compatibility with Python 2.4 (Civ4 engine constraint)

Reuses the AI_AGGREGATE_SCORES dictionary with no change to rendering logic

🧪 Performance Note
This change adds no noticeable runtime cost. Even with:

~53 leaders

~30 aggregates

= ~1600 comparisons

The cost is negligible (~1–2ms), and all scores are cached once at startup.

🔮 Future Ideas & Suggestions
Visual Hinting in Tooltips
Show percentile label like "Top 10%" or "Bottom 25%" on hover

Apply Percentiles to Individual Attributes
So the same fair distribution applies to every XML trait (not just aggregates)

Weight Aggregates Differently
Allow traits like getMaxWarRand to count more heavily for "Aggressive"

Color-Based Visualization
Green for peaceful, red for aggressive, based on percentile score

Leader Comparison View
Let players compare two leaders side by side

🎯 Why This Matters
Players and modders can now:

Trust the scores they see

Spot meaningful differences between leaders

Interpret behaviors more accurately in-game

Use this system as a foundation for more advanced AI documentation, tutorials, and meta-analysis

This also creates a cleaner data path if you later decide to tune AI personalities, as percentile-based aggregates will better show the impact of any XML tweaks.

🙌 Final Words
This change:

Preserves the layout and style you worked hard to build

Enhances clarity and precision without complexity

Reflects how players intuitively think about leader differences

In short: it’s both more accurate and more human-readable. 🧠📊

Enjoy!

✅ Git Commit Message:
Optimize aggregate AI personality trait scores via module-level caching (Sevopedia performance boost)

🧠 Summary
This commit introduces module-level caching of aggregate AI personality scores for each leader. The scores are now computed once at module load time and stored in a dictionary (AI_AGGREGATE_SCORES). This improves Sevopedia performance, eliminates redundant computation, and keeps the codebase cleaner.

🎓 For New Modders or Players
Instead of computing every detail of a leader’s behavior whenever you open their Sevopedia page, we now summarize these behaviors ahead of time and store them. These summaries are high-level traits like:

"Aggressive"

"Peaceful"

"Builder"

"Sneaky"

"Stingy"

This makes the AI Personality panel faster and lighter, even if you're flipping through multiple leaders quickly.

👩‍🏫 Analogy: Grading Students in a Class
Imagine you’re a teacher with 40 students and each has grades in 20 subjects. If you had to recalculate their average every time you view their profile, it would be slow and repetitive.

Instead, we now compute all the students’ averages once at the start and save them. Later, you just look up the result. This is exactly what we’re doing here for AI leaders.

📊 Technical Insight: Why This Matters
Previously, every time you opened a leader page, the game would:

Loop through all 44 leaders

For each aggregate (30+ total), look up ~3 raw XML values

Normalize the selected leader’s values against all others

Compute the average

This resulted in ~1200 integer reads per page load (44 leaders × 30 traits approx.), just for the aggregate score computation.

Even though reading 1200 integers is not huge by modern standards, it's:

Completely redundant (the data never changes)

Performed every time a leader page opens

Adds lag or stutter especially on older systems or laptops

Now, with this caching:

We compute these ~1200 values once

Store them in a small Python dictionary (AI_AGGREGATE_SCORES)

Lookup becomes O(1) and instantaneous

The memory cost is negligible:

44 leaders × 30 traits = 1320 integers

That’s ~5 KB total, which is trivial for any machine running Civ4

🧑‍💻 For Advanced Devs
Introduced global constant:

python
Copy
Edit
AI_AGGREGATE_SCORES = {}  # iLeader -> { label: normalized_score }
Added cache_ai_aggregate_scores() which:

Iterates over gc.getNumLeaderHeadInfos()

Computes all aggregates for each leader using existing logic

Stores the normalized scores using already-cached min/max ranges in AI_VALUE_RANGES

Updated placeAIPersonalityPanel() to directly access:

python
Copy
Edit
score = AI_AGGREGATE_SCORES[iLeader][label]
Preserves structure, logic, and layout. Only the source of scores is optimized.

⚡ Performance Impact
Instant lookup of aggregate scores

Panel draws faster and with less CPU overhead

Avoids redundant Python list construction, function calls, and math

Maintains the same output (no visual changes)

🧼 Bonus Improvements
Removed redundant list comprehension (values = [...]) inside scoring logic

Ensured tab-based indentation for full Civ4 compatibility

Clean separation of data collection (at load time) from UI rendering (on demand)

📚 Future Suggestions
Consider caching the string labels of traits and aggregates too

Could reuse these scores in advisor screens, tooltips, diplomacy insights, etc.

Enables potential comparison tools (showing how leaders differ at a glance)

ChatGPT Breakdown below:

✅ Commit Title
Optimize AI Personality Panel by caching XML value ranges at module load

📘 Overview
This commit introduces a significant performance and clarity enhancement to the AI Personality panel in the Sevopedia Leader page. The panel previously recalculated AI XML value ranges (min/max) for every leader view, leading to unnecessary computational overhead. These values are now computed once at module load and cached globally, resulting in faster UI rendering and better separation of logic.

🔍 Why this change?
Performance optimization:
Leader AI XML values (e.g., getMaxWarRand, getTechTradeKnownPercent, etc.) are static for the entire game session. Previously, each time a leader was opened in the Sevopedia, the system recomputed these values across all leaders — for every single AI trait and aggregate.
By caching once at load time, we remove this redundant work and speed up rendering on every page access.

Cleaner, more maintainable logic:
Centralizing normalization ranges in a dictionary (AI_VALUE_RANGES) simplifies downstream code — each normalization call now requires only the function name, rather than raw lists or recomputation logic. This improves clarity and maintainability.

Improved scalability:
If more AI attributes or aggregate behaviors are added (which is the plan), this approach allows those to be integrated without scaling up computational load during page rendering.

🔧 What was changed
New Global Dictionary: AI_VALUE_RANGES

Stores (min, max) tuples for every AI attribute getter function used in both AI_ATTRIBUTE_CATEGORIES and AI_AGGREGATES.

Precomputed once at module load by iterating over all leader XML entries.

Supports automatic expansion if new attributes are added.

Updated placeAIPersonalityPanel function:

Removes all real-time min/max calculations.

Simplifies normalize() function — it now only uses cached values.

Removes redundant or unused variable computations like:

python
Copy
Edit
values = [getattr(gc.getLeaderHeadInfo(i), funcName)() for i in range(numLeaders)]
Improves readability and function weight, while keeping compatibility with Civ4’s Python 2.4 environment.

No visual changes to users, but responsiveness is improved on slower machines or large mods with many leaders.

🛠️ How to use / integrate
Make sure AI_VALUE_RANGES is computed after defining AI_ATTRIBUTE_CATEGORIES and AI_AGGREGATES. It must be placed at the module level (outside the class) so it's built once and reused.

Example placement:

python
Copy
Edit
AI_VALUE_RANGES = {}
for i in range(gc.getNumLeaderHeadInfos()):
	...
📚 Future improvements / suggestions
Aggregate score caching (optional):
Similar logic can be extended to cache aggregate scores per leader as a secondary step, especially useful if symbols or visualizations become more elaborate.

Symbol rendering types:
Color-coding or symbol types could adapt based on the behavior type (e.g., threatening vs. diplomatic).

Refactor cache building into a dedicated function
If this grows in complexity, abstracting the cache build process can improve code reuse and visibility for modders.

👥 Audience Notes
For new contributors:
You don’t need to worry about recomputing stats. Just update the attribute or aggregate lists, and the system will automatically use cached min/max ranges.

For experienced developers:
This lays the foundation for more responsive dynamic Pedia UIs, even in mods with 50+ leaders. It avoids GC and function call overhead per frame and provides structure for more advanced visualizations later.

python

python

for idx, (label, fields) in enumerate(AI_AGGREGATES):

Refactored AI aggregate definitions into class-level constants for clarity and performance

This commit moves the `aggregates` and `ai_attribute_categories` dictionaries from the `placeAIPersonalityPanel` method into class-level variables (`AGGREGATES` and `AI_ATTRIBUTE_CATEGORIES`) in SevoPediaLeader.py.

These structures define which AI XML values are used for each aggregate trait (like "Aggressive" or "Sneaky") and group them into categories for visual organization. By moving them to the class level, we:
- Avoid recomputing or redefining them every time a new leader is viewed in the Sevopedia
- Keep the data in one clear location for easy editing, debugging, and extension
- Improve readability and make the logic reusable in other parts of the Sevopedia if needed later

This is part of an ongoing effort to improve performance and modularity of the AI Personality panel, while staying true to the game's Python 2.4 style and Civ4 modding conventions. Constants are written in UPPER_CASE for clarity, even if this differs slightly from other parts of Sevopedia code.

myself but anyways..., thanks etc anyways, thanks,):

Yes, absolutely — you can and should move the aggregates list to __init__ if you're aiming for cleaner, more optimized, and modular code, especially since:

It's a static definition: The list of aggregates and their associated XML keys don't change dynamically per leader, so it's perfectly valid to define them once during __init__.

It mirrors what you already did with self.ai_attribute_categories, centralizing configuration for readability and reuse.

It will slightly improve performance, since the list doesn't get redefined every time placeAIPersonalityPanel is called.

Now to your question about the AI attribute dictionary and whether to move it to __init__:

✅ Should you move it to __init__?
Yes — it can be a good idea. Here's why:

📌 Pros:
Improved performance (slightly): The dictionary is only built once per screen instance instead of every time the placeAIPersonalityPanel function is called.

Cleaner function logic: You reduce clutter in placeAIPersonalityPanel and treat the dictionary as a persistent config.

Centralization: Easier to maintain or update the attribute definitions if they’re all declared in one place, especially if you're going to reuse this dictionary later (e.g., filtering, sorting, exporting, etc).

⚠️ Possible Cons / Risks:
Out-of-sync risks: If the dictionary ever needs to change dynamically depending on the leader (unlikely), you'd risk having stale data unless it’s rebuilt each time.

Memory use: Minor, since it’s a static structure and lives for the life of the screen. But if you instantiate a lot of screens (you don’t), this could matter.

✅ Verdict:
In your case — where the data is fixed and only used in the leader screen — moving it to __init__ is a clean and efficient refactor.

commit 12cf735251ed3efdeb62a0c10f56cf3483c122d2
Author: f1rpo <hidden>
Date:   2025-03-23 16:07:16 +0100

Take back more of the city billboard enlargement

Previously adjusted by this commit: 03e2ecee79be5ac8b52873f13b99c473f8eaf4ef

Related CFC post (2nd half):
https://forums.civfanatics.com/threads/taurus.677586/post-16797663

Having tried higher field-of-view values: The FoV does not affect the billboard sizes, which means that, at a higher FoV value, the billboards look large compared with tiles. Worse, players will then likely play at a closer camera distance, meaning that the higher scale factors for medium camera distances apply. While AdvCiv disables the FoV slider by default (and thereby encourages players to keep the BtS value), some players will still adjust the value and, then, the result is too unappealing with my earlier settings. The scale for far distances isn't the main issue, but the idea of magnifying rather quickly when zooming in isn't workable. [advc.002b]

commit 7c420a132949a1853e9beaf7e60548d99b8fbd4c
Author: codingnewcode <hidden>
Date:   2025-03-22 18:36:31 +0100

alter the tech priorities to focus more on military and early growth

To give AI a better start, give it more (or make it value more) some earlier
techs, especially growth techs and military techs. Some techs are also
particularly less valued now (archery is not versatile enough to be of
use to the AI early i think).
History relevance (see feudalism and machinery free tech code changes at higher
difficulties) does not matter to me (and should be less effective) than choosing
the strongest/a stronger possible strategy.

See the detail below:

These techs should be more valuable early:
- bronze working: to upgrade the defending warriors sooner, and to reveale
copper sooner for better city placement (and tile yields), as well as ressource
commerce sooner (but commerce should not be too important too soon, just an extra
advantage)
- animal husbandry: similar reasons as bronze working, the special unit is the chariot
though
- pottery: less important than the first two, but should help to build cottages sooner
or start a granary sooner where it is more relevant
- mysticism and fishing: not extremely important but i think they would work better
as free techs at higher difficulties, as they are not expansive, but the AI can
capitalize on these techs sooner (work boats, monuments, stonehedge, moai, etc.) if
they are freely available.

These techs should be less valuable early:
- iron working: not good enough as a starter tech, bronze working (+/- animal
husbandry) for the reasons explained above in the point about these techs
- sailing as done in advciv, but it should not be a too big concern if AI starts
with sailing too soon, so i reduced the iWeight.

These techs should be much less valuable early:
- archery: unless AI is lagging behind on military power or/adn starting to turtle,
archers are less effective at offense (than other similar-close priced units (mainly
chariots and spearmen and axemen) (so quite bad at early rushes) and also cannot be
upgraded from free warriors at higher difficulties (so not as fast to build than a
stack of axemen-spearmen-swordsmen in comparison).
It may even be possible to skip it entirely, especially if AI is military stronger, the
archers then would not help it so much. Maybe wait until longbowmen are available to
reevaluate the need then, or produce other more offensive units as a more versatile
strategy.
